correctness.rationale: The reciprocal biomass map is affine with positive intercept and two-step slope 1/(r₀r₁S). For positive initial data this gives attraction to a unique positive cycle iff Q>0 and extinction otherwise, including linear growth of reciprocal biomass at Q=0. Solving the affine cycle gives the supplied two biomasses; post-recruitment catch equals (1−s_i)x_{i+1}/s_i. Write N(t)=K₁+r₀K₀t and D(t)=r₁SK₁+K₀t. The derivative of normalized catch has the sign of R−N/D, and (N/D)'=QK₀K₁/D²>0. Thus the two clipped cases and the unique interior critical point include endpoint derivative equality; in the interior r₀−R=QK₁/D(t*)>0. For regret, set L=K₀+r₁SK₁ and H=(K₁+r₀SK₀)/S. The normalized yield difference between t and t* is (t−t*)[H/(N(t)N(t*))−L/(D(t)D(t*))]. Insert H/N(t*)²=L/D(t*)² and use N(t*)D(t)−D(t*)N(t)=−QK₀K₁(t−t*) to recover the exact strictly positive prefactor of (t−t*)². The regret identity is for interior t* only; uniqueness is only for Q>0. Independent bounded arithmetic gives 44/7 versus 3.746394253408705 in the endpoint example.
residual_risks: Extinction gives zero limiting yield for every allocation. The positive two-cycle attracts positive starts, not the invariant zero state.

The supported distinct claim is the fixed-product constrained optimizer, including both corner regimes, and exact interior regret. This is a bounded best-of-knowledge finding.

value.rationale: Two seasonal fleets with the same total log mortality can have the same persistence verdict yet appreciably different long-run catches. The explicit allocation boundary distinguishes a genuine corner from an interior split, and an exact all-feasible-deviations loss is more informative than a local second derivative or an unconstrained optimum. The result is a useful deterministic benchmark, not a general harvest prescription.
residual_risks: No operational fishing recommendation follows without uncertainty, prices and ecological constraints; no claim is made for more than two seasons or optimization over aggregate mortality.
